pathAudit.conclusion: Relationship-type words are many-to-one summaries of paths. They do not determine endpoints, scientific signatures or an ALE valuation.

directExtraction.reason: The relationship capture is an epistemic directed graph, not a collection of ScientificTransformation records. Supplying uniform opaque signatures, zero dimensions, synthetic evidence and positional rule IDs would be a programmable completion, not extraction.

semanticCollision.Challenges: A Claimipedia challenge is an authored epistemic relation. A failed Sourcery transformation is excluded from the admitted category and retained in a rejection receipt; it is not a negative composable edge.
semanticCollision.Supports: Support does not state a scientific operation, its endpoint signature changes or its irreversible information loss.
semanticCollision.Qualifies: Qualification does not determine projection, continuation, transport or update semantics.
semanticCollision.DependsOn: Dependency does not distinguish an assumption token from evidence, a required object, a computational prerequisite or a causal transformation.

decision.classification: exact source-native no-go for direct typed extraction from the pinned relationship capture

reopenGate: Expose stable authored relationship IDs rather than relying on capture position.
Type every participating claim as a scientific object with exact signature and dimension metadata.
Classify each edge as a scientific transformation or retain it outside the admitted path category as an epistemic relation.
Attach declared changes, assumptions, irreversible losses, evidence references, analogy status and bounded authority.
Admit at least one nontrivial path through the unchanged Sourcery protocol and predict a held-out composition, product identity or detector record.
boundary: The common object is a directed path skeleton plus provenance of the capture. Claimipedia's epistemic relation algebra and Sourcery's typed scientific-transformation category are not the same algebra. No Jordan, Lie, physical or authority-bearing structure follows from the graph-only overlap.
